questions.question: When should you inspect your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. Small problems on a motorcycle can be more dangerous than on a car.

questions.question: Your friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
Get other friends to convince them not to ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get other friends to convince them not to ride.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone to ride after drinking. Stop them any way you can. Get your friends to help talk them out of riding.

questions.question: When alcohol and drugs are used together, what happens?

options.text: Their combined effects are stronger than using either alone.
They are less dangerous than using either alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Their combined effects are stronger than using either alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including over-the-counter and prescription medications, can affect your riding ability. Mixing drugs with alcohol makes the danger much worse.

questions.question: Why are turn signals important on a motorcycle?

options.text: They serve little purpose since motorcycles are small.
They warn other drivers what you plan to do.
You should not use them if no vehicles are nearby.
They are more complicated than car signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: They warn other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: As a motorcycle rider, you are very vulnerable. Always use your turn signals when changing lanes or turning, even if you think no one else is nearby.

questions.question: Intersections are usually:

options.text: Safe because there is lots of traffic.

questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous because many accidents happen there between motorcyclists and other drivers.

questions.question: What color are warning signs?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the best protection when riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the most protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT important when choosing a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: It meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
It fits snugly around your entire head.
It has no cracks, loose padding, or damage.

questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet U.S. DOT standards, fit snugly all around your head, and have no cracks or damage. How it looks does not matter for safety.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: You do not need a head check if you use your mirrors.
Your mirrors show everything around your motorcycle.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Assume drivers will respond correctly to your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol, what should you do?

options.text: Decide if you can ride based on how you feel.
Set a limit so you can still ride safely.
Do not worry if you feel fine.

questions.explanation: Do not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol. Even small amounts can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: For the best protection, wear a helmet that:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no defects.

questions.question: For the best protection, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Be loose and flap in the wind while riding.
Only partially cover your arms and legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should cover your arms and legs completely for protection while riding. They should fit snugly but allow you to move freely. Leather or synthetic materials provide the best protection in an accident.

questions.question: What types of brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake provides more braking power than the rear brake.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should a motorcyclist do to prevent injury?
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, decrease your speed. Sudden moves could cause your motorcycle to skid. Do not ride on the shoulder to avoid slippery roads.

questions.question: Turn signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Are even more important than signals on cars and trucks.
Should not be used unless another vehicle is right next to you.
Are less important than signals on cars and trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are even more important than signals on cars and trucks.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists are more vulnerable than car and truck drivers. Because of this, using turn signals is even more important for motorcyclists.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a dangerously slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid a dangerously slippery surface, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: The shortest and safest stops happen when you:

options.text: Let the front tire lock up.
Use both the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes in a smooth, controlled way to achieve the shortest and safest stops. Do not let either tire skid.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of having an accident, you should:

options.text: Blend into traffic and not be noticed by other drivers.
Not use turn signals unless you are riding at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
Ride closely behind the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to other drivers. Use your turn signals, brake light, and proper lane position to show your intentions. Keep a safe distance from other vehicles, look ahead 12 seconds, and be ready to act if a hazard appears.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator?
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handgrip and is controlled with the right hand.

questions.question: Riding gloves are often made of:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riding gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: Regular motorcycle maintenance helps because:

options.text: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
questions.explanation: A well-maintained motorcycle will ride like new if you do regular maintenance checks.

questions.question: When riding at night:

options.text: Wear reflective clothing to be more visible.
Other drivers cannot see your turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear reflective clothing to be more visible.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials when riding at night so other drivers can see you better.

questions.question: A motorcycle operator can slow down by:
questions.explanation: Downshifting slows down a motorcycle. Note that downshifting does not turn on your brake lights.

questions.question: Before riding your motorcycle, check all of the following except:

options.text: Both brake controls activate the brake light.

questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil, fluids, and all lights: headlight, taillight, signal lights, and brake light.

questions.question: A plastic face shield protects the rider from:
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your face from wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, pebbles, and injury in a crash.
